ISO 21423 sets a common communication basis for mixed robot fleets

The interoperability standard covers robots, fleet managers and building systems; it is not a safety certification.

The Robot Report ↗3 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

A basis for mixed fleets

A November 3 report says A3 announced ISO 21423:2026 the previous day. Developed by ISO Technical Committee 299, it addresses communication and interoperability between industrial mobile robots such as AGVs and AMRs from different suppliers. Publication does not mean every vendor already supports it.

Exchanging state and requests

The standard defines exchanges and action requests between robots, fleet managers and other equipment. Information includes location, speed, direction, condition, tasks and availability. A3 expects fewer path conflicts and better efficiency, but the report provides no universal throughput or return-on-investment result.

Beyond robot-to-robot communication

The scope includes tended machines, ERP systems, lifts, automatic doors and alarms, as well as people’s mobile or wearable devices. This is a non-safety standard. Buyers still need to establish actual implementation support and assess site safety separately before connecting mixed fleets.
